answer: Each agent must deposit a refundable stake that is locked until it contributes a unique comet-style proof of sequential work whose difficulty scales with total network size. The stake is only returned after the agent has validated a random subset of prior ocean-delta cross-checks performed by other agents; an attacker spawning many identities therefore locks capital equal to the number of fakes and must keep paying ongoing compute for the sequential proofs, so the cost of a sybil campaign grows linearly with headcount.
